hobbies to make you
disgustingly intelligent

reading old maps

study an old map of your city once a week and compare it to today. you'll learn history, geography and urban planning all at once, almost by accident.

learning sign language

learn ten signs a week in your local sign language. a new kind of language rewires how you think about words, and it lets you speak with people you never could before.

a daily lesson

spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in a field you've never studied: geology, music theory, ancient law. tiny lessons in odd subjects build a remarkably wide mind.

a daily lesson

i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in a field i never studied: geology, music theory, ancient law. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and my mind got remarkably wide.

slides.texte_overlay:
debating at dinner

pick one big question at dinner with friends, like is free will real, and argue it out kindly. good debates sharpen your thinking faster than any book alone.

writing book summaries

after every book, write a one page summary from memory. it shows you what actually stuck, and it roughly doubles how much of each book you remember months later.
